key_insight: An agentic LLM system can translate natural-language questions into accurate, auditable statistical analyses of TCGA clinical data by choosing among specialized tools instead of relying on one-shot generation.
clinical_relevance: This could make large cancer clinical repositories easier to query for researchers and support faster, more transparent exploratory analysis with source-backed answers.
method: ReAct LLM agent routes each query to one of 8 tools
Tools include data extraction, descriptive stats, Kaplan-Meier survival, log-rank testing, and hypothesis testing
Answers are checked against the curated TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource with traceable outputs
evidence_signal: On TCGA-Agent-Bench (440 queries), the system reached 93.4% overall accuracy, outperforming a rule-based pipeline, a single-pass LLM, and retrieval-augmented generation; it also answered 100% of 26 queries involving fields missing from the CDR versus 3.8% for CDR-only.
watch_item: Performance may depend on tool coverage and curated reference quality, so deployment still needs careful validation, especially for fields not present in the benchmark source.
paper_title: A ReAct Agentic AI System for Natural Language Querying and Statistical Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas Clinical Data
